name: mcp-secrets-runner
stderr:
mcp-secrets-runner: start an MCP server with secrets injected from a secret manager

Usage:
  mcp-secrets-runner [--provider=<name>] [provider flags...] -- <mcp server command>
  mcp-secrets-runner doctor [--provider=<name>] [--offline]

Example (.mcp.json):
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "stripe": {
        "type": "stdio",
        "command": "npx",
        "args": ["-y", "mcp-secrets-runner", "--env=prod", "--path=/mcp",
                 "--", "npx", "-y", "@stripe/mcp@latest"]
      }
    }
  }

Commands:
  doctor              check the CLI, credentials, instance and secret path without
                      starting a server (--offline skips the authentication test)

Options:
  --provider=<name>   secret backend to use (default: infisical,
                      or $MCP_SECRETS_PROVIDER)
  --no-token-cache    mint a fresh token instead of reusing a cached one
  -h, --help          show this help
  -v, --version       show version

Providers:
  infisical (default)
    Auth:  INFISICAL_UA_CLIENT_ID + INFISICAL_UA_CLIENT_SECRET  (machine identity, Universal Auth)
    Also:  INFISICAL_DOMAIN       instance URL, overrides .infisical.json
           INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID   overrides workspaceId from .infisical.json
           INFISICAL_BIN          path to the infisical binary if it is not on PATH
    Flags before -- are passed to `infisical run` (e.g. --env=prod --path=/mcp)

  1password
    Auth:  OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN  (service account; a CLI/desktop session also works but expires)
    Also:  OP_BIN                    path to the op binary if it is not on PATH
    Flags before -- are passed to `op run` (e.g. --env-file=./mcp.env)
    Secrets are op:// references, resolved by op run.

  vault
    Auth:  VAULT_ROLE_ID + VAULT_SECRET_ID  (AppRole), or VAULT_TOKEN
    Also:  VAULT_ADDR       instance URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8200)
           VAULT_NAMESPACE  namespace header, for Vault Enterprise / HCP
    Flags: --path=<path>    secret to read (required)
           --mount=<mount>  KV mount (default: secret)
           --kv-version=1|2 KV engine version (default: 2)
    Reads the secret over the HTTP API; no Vault CLI required.
